clue.text: Scorer managed, in absentia, football team's home success

indicators.note: being absent means the letters of the word for managed are missing from the team name

parts.note: Rangers is a Glasgow football club, nicknamed the Gers
managed means ran, as in ran a business
H is a common abbreviation for home, as in football results
a success is a win

explanation.surface: A goalscorer, despite the manager being away, secures a victory at the team's home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' looks like a footballer but means a composer who writes scores. RANGERS is a Scottish football club; removing RAN leaves its nickname GERS.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin wrote musical scores, so he is a composer, a writer of scores.

clue.text: Strove in speech with moral excellence for US city

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the past tense of the verb for strove is heard as a word for a stronghold

parts.note: strove means fought, struggled
worth is merit or moral excellence

explanation.surface: Someone talks of struggling for virtue on behalf of an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort Worth is a large city in Texas, next to Dallas.

clue.text: Has dances confined by eg square dance movement

indicators.note: being confined by means the letters sit inside the word for eg

parts.note: eg, for example, can be rendered as say

indicators.note: dances signals the letters of has are jiggled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has dances restricted to, for instance, a square dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dances' looks like a verb about the dancer, but it only signals rearranging; 'eg' gives SAY, the container.
explanation.definitionFit: In square dancing a sashay is a gliding sideways step, one of the called figures.

clue.text: Month spent with Dr Werewolf, whence 13 15?

indicators.note: spent, as in used up and exhausted, signals the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor who is a werewolf passes a month, which prompts the question of where something came from.
explanation.walkthrough: MONTH and DR WEREWOLF together have fifteen letters to rearrange. Gershwin's An American in Paris features an American, someone from the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: An American comes from the Americas, the New World, so a riddling question about origin fits; the phrase is also Dvorak's symphony title.

clue.text: Member employed to split the opposition?

definitions.text: Member employed to split the opposition?

parts.words: Member employed to split the opposition?
parts.note: member is a limb; the one used to cut an opponent apart in a fight is the arm that wields the blade

explanation.surface: Someone is brought in to divide the political opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a member of a party and 'opposition' a political one; really a limb that hacks enemies apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm that holds the sword is the limb used to cut down an enemy in combat.

clue.text: Ham actor, losing lead, is put off love

indicators.note: off, as in gone off or awry, signals the combined letters are rearranged
losing its lead means the word actor drops its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: An actor who has lost a leading role is discouraged from romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing lead' turns ACTOR into CTOR; with IS PUT and O these ten letters are rearranged by 'off'. 'Ham actor' looks like one phrase, but 'Ham' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosciutto is a type of Italian cured ham, served thinly sliced.

clue.text: Force Faith to eat hat (just the top)

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so the word for faith goes around the letter

parts.note: faith means trust

indicators.note: just the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone forced to eat their hat, but only the brim.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrust is a forceful push, so force works as a synonym for it as a noun.

clue.text: Jaunty, emergent person broadcasting

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman emerging into society
a programme that is broadcasting is on air

explanation.surface: A cheerful newcomer is presenting on radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a confident, stylish and carefree manner, close to jaunty.

clue.text: See 2
Platinum-coated vessel that is said to gain attention on the quiet

definitions.text: said to gain attention on the quiet

indicators.note: coated means the platinum letters wrap around the outside

parts.note: PT is the chemical symbol for platinum
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship plated with precious metal is said to attract notice discreetly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the hissing whisper used to catch someone's attention without making a noise.

clue.text: Nuts queue hours (not OK socially) to catch premiere of major work of 22 across

indicators.note: catching something holds it inside, so the scrambled letters go around the letter
nuts, meaning crazy, signals the letters are scrambled
not means the letter for socially acceptable is taken out

parts.note: U means upper-class and hence socially acceptable, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: the premiere of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A crazy, lengthy queue, socially awkward, to see the opening of a great composer's masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U is a British idea of upper-class versus common usage, so U means socially OK; 'not' drops one U before 'Nuts' rearranges the rest, and 'to catch' puts M inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dvorak wrote a famous set of Humoresques for piano, so this is a work by that composer.

clue.text: Waste fluid and Sweeney's foot dripping

indicators.note: fluid, meaning flowing and changeable, signals the letters are rearranged
the foot of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Sweeney's foot oozes waste fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste fluid' looks like one phrase; 'fluid' is the anagram signal. The Sweeney was a British TV police drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is sweaty is dripping with perspiration.

clue.text: 1's work could be, say, Warhol at the Louvre?

definitions.meaning: a piece composed by Gershwin, the answer at 1 down

definitions.text: could be, say, Warhol at the Louvre?
definitions.meaning: Andy Warhol was from the United States, and the Louvre is the great museum in the French capital

explanation.surface: A composer's piece imagines a pop artist visiting a famous French museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin's tone poem, and also a literal description of a US citizen visiting the French capital.

clue.text: Bucket on TV bulb

definitions.meaning: Mrs Bucket, the snobbish lead of the British sitcom Keeping Up Appearances, insists her name is pronounced Bouquet
a spring-flowering plant grown from a bulb

explanation.surface: A pail appears on television beside a lightbulb.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom character's first name, and a fragrant flower grown from a bulb.

clue.text: See 13
Rudimentary travelling to China on back of horse

indicators.note: travelling suggests movement, so the letters are moved around
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for China on horseback in a primitive way.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means just begun and not yet fully formed, hence rudimentary.

clue.text: Setter's just the thing, having polished off ape

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so setter's is I am, I'm
just the thing is it, as in that's it
polished off food means ate it

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being perfect after finishing off a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polished off' sounds like killing the ape, but it means ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy or mimic them.

clue.text: Restraints of public transport around one third of the city

indicators.note: around means the vehicles go round the shortened city

parts.note: trams are a form of public transport

indicators.note: one third of the nine-letter city name is its first three letters

parts.note: Melbourne, the Australian city known for its trams

explanation.surface: Trams circle a part of the city, holding things back.
explanation.definitionFit: Trammels are things that hamper or restrict freedom of movement.

clue.text: Has to undergo housing shock

indicators.note: housing means the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone must have an operation in a care home, a nasty shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to shock or amaze greatly.

clue.text: City, central European situation, tops for perfumery ingredients

parts.note: Essen is a city in western Germany

indicators.note: the tops of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A German city's central position supplies the makings of scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Essences are concentrated extracts used in making perfumes.

clue.text: Adder stretch standard from 1

parts.note: an adder is one who adds up figures, a summer
a stretch is a period of time

explanation.surface: A snake stretches out as the measuring rule of the composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adder' looks like a snake; it is one who adds, a SUMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin's song from Porgy and Bess became one of the most recorded jazz standards.

clue.text: Dark, sad, very oxygen-enriched creator of 4 26

indicators.note: enriched means the letters are added into the middle of the scrambled word
sad, in the sense of sorry or poor, signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A gloomy, melancholy figure is enriched with oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad' rearranges DARK to DRAK, and VO goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonin Dvorak composed the symphony that the linked entries name.

clue.text: Lives in blue abandon

indicators.note: in means the word for lives goes inside

parts.note: blue means sad, down
lives means exists, is

explanation.surface: Someone lives in melancholy and gives up hope.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to reject or abandon them.

clue.text: Unfussy as a consumer, Novello's put in one-off threatening surroundings

indicators.note: put in means the name is placed inside the trimmed word
surroundings means the trimmed word goes around the name
off means the letter for one is removed

parts.note: threatening means ominous
I is the Roman numeral for one
Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor

explanation.surface: Novello is placed in a single sinister setting, eating anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-off' looks like a single word meaning unique, but it splits: 'one' is I and 'off' removes it, leaving OMNOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivorous creature eats all kinds of food, plant and animal, so it is not fussy.

clue.text: See 21
God — soften sound!

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to soften ice is to thaw it

explanation.surface: A deity declares that something should become gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse god of thunder.

clue.text: Force out? That's nice

definitions.meaning: to extract something by force, as a payment or confession
nice in its old sense means precise or fine

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether force should be used, then says it is pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact as a verb means to demand by force; as an adjective it means precise.
